'''Jun Wen''' ({{zh|s=文军}}, Born December 27, 1963) is an evolutionary biologist and curator at the [[Smithsonian]]'s [[National Museum of Natural History]] in the Department of Botany and has worked in the Laboratory of Molecular Systematics. She researches the monography, phylogenetics, biogeography, and ethnobotany of the plant families [[Araliaceae]] and [[Vitaceae]]. She has published over 190 scientific papers.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://biogenomics.si.edu/profile/jun-wen|title=Jun Wen {{!}} Institute for Biogenomics Diversity|website=biogenomics.si.edu|language=en|access-date=2018-08-17}}</ref>

== Life and career ==
Jun Wen was born on 27 December in 1963 in [[Hubei, China]]. in 1984 she graduated from the [[Huazhong Agricultural University|Central China Agricultural University]] (Also known as [[Huazhong Agricultural University]]) with a BS in Forestry. She attended [[Ohio State University]] and received a PhD in Biology in 1991. She completed a postdoctoral position at the [[Arnold Arboretum]] at [[Harvard University]] in 1994 and then moved to the Smithsonian for a postdoctoral fellowship. She was appointed as an assistant professor and curator of the herbarium at [[Colorado State University]] in the Department of Biology in 1995. She became an associate curator for [[Field Museum of Natural History|The Field Museum]] in [[Chicago|Chicago, Illinois]], in 2000 and remained there more 5 years. In 2005 she was hired at the Smithsonian's National Museum of Natural History as a research botanist and curator in the Department of Botany.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.linkedin.com/in/jun-wen-3539776|title=Jun Wen|last=Wen|first=Jun|date=|website=LinkedIn|access-date=}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=October 2019|title=Jun Wen|url=https://wbfc.science/single/?smid=401|access-date=2021-03-25|website=Washington Biologists' Field Club}}</ref>

Wen has studied the world's oldest grape fossils while investigating the evolutionary history of the [[Vitaceae|modern grape family]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=2013-11-15|title=World's oldest-known grape fossils found in India|url=https://www.floridamuseum.ufl.edu/science/worlds-oldest-known-grape-fossils-found-in-india/|access-date=2020-07-30|website=Florida Museum|language=en-US}}</ref>

Wen was as the treasurer of the [[American Society of Plant Taxonomists]] and in the finance section as an officer from 2006 to 2009.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web|title=ASPT Officers & Committees|url=http://wwn.inhs.illinois.edu/~kenr/ASPT/officers.html|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180817193352/http://wwn.inhs.illinois.edu/~kenr/ASPT/officers.html|archive-date=2018-08-17|access-date=2018-08-17|website=wwn.inhs.illinois.edu}}</ref> She was a council member of the International Association of Plant Taxonomists, a co-Editor-in-Chief of the ''Journal of Systematics and Evolution'',<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://nmnh.typepad.com/the_plant_press/2015/11/wen-joins-editorial-board-of-journal-of-systematics-and-evolution.html|title=Wen Joins Editorial Board of Journal of Systematics and Evolution - The Plant Press|website=nmnh.typepad.com|access-date=2018-08-17}}</ref> and on many committees for several other societies. She was elected into the Washington Biologists' Field Club in 2009.<ref name=":0" /> In 2006 she was a guest professor at the [[Kunming Institute of Botany]] of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] for a 4-year appointment.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://nmnh.typepad.com/the_plant_press/2006/07/plant-press-2006-vol-9-issue-3-9.html|title=Awards and Grants - The Plant Press|website=nmnh.typepad.com|access-date=2018-08-17}}</ref> Wen and fellow botanists endorsed the Shenzhen Declaration in 2017, calling for plant sciences to contribute to sustainability efforts.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Connecting plants and society: The Shenzhen Declaration, a new roadmap for plant sciences|url=https://www.eurekalert.org/pub_releases/2017-09/pp-cpa091817.php|access-date=2020-07-30|website=EurekAlert!|language=en}}</ref>

Wen works to inspire interest in science in young people. She is part of the Smithsonian's internship program called Youth Engagement Through Science (YES!) where she works with interns in high school and college to have hand-on experience and instruction.<ref name=":0" />
